Definition: to select; to feed; to render clear
BiblicalUsage: Barah means to choose, to select, and also to feed, to prepare food for someone. Goliath calls Israel to choose a man to fight him, David's servants beg him to eat bread and he refuses while his child is sick, and Amnon asks for Tamar to come and make food before his eyes.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word shows how small choices carry great weight, because a chosen champion decides a battle and a prepared meal hides a wicked plan. David would not eat while he pleaded for his son, and I hold that his fasting says more about his heart than any words could.
RelatedPeople: King David; Amnon, Son of David
